title: AUTH-3 contact-frequency boundary returns LIMIT_EXCEEDED instead of silently dropping
risk: A reminder storm contacts the same customer three or more times because the cap is applied as a soft drop rather than a typed refusal, or the cap silently blocks legitimate transactional messages.
preconditions: Namespace gov-unit-auth-<case_id>-<worker_id>; no shared mutable state with other cases.
PolicyEnforcementPoint loaded with fixtures/offline/governance.json skill_authority_registry and agents[]; clock frozen at 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z.
Synthetic cap maxAutonomousReminderCount=2 for T1 (design parameter, not an approved limit).

steps.action: Send two permitted transactional messages to cust-a
steps.expected: Both return PERMIT and the adapter counter reaches 2.

steps.action: Send a third transactional message to the same customer in the same window
steps.expected: Verdict is LIMIT_EXCEEDED with a retry-after or window hint; the adapter counter stays at 2.

steps.action: Send a marketing message to cust-b (opt-out in the consents fixture)
steps.expected: Verdict is suppressed for consent, which is a different decision code from LIMIT_EXCEEDED so operators can tell the causes apart.
Four rows: two success, one limit-exceeded, one consent-suppressed, each with a distinct decision code.

assertions: The cap is enforced at exactly 2 within the window and the boundary is inclusive of the second message.
LIMIT_EXCEEDED and consent suppression are distinguishable decision codes, not one generic error.
Adapter counter is 2, never 3, proving the third message was not delivered.
No message is silently dropped without an audit row and a typed verdict.
forbidden: Counting a limit-blocked message as delivered.
Applying the marketing consent check to transactional messages and breaking order notifications.
Resetting the counter so a retry storm bypasses the cap.
evidence: PEP decision JSON for the four attempts.
Adapter counter and the four audit rows.
cleanup: Reset the gov- reminder counters and delete the run namespace; no message was actually delivered.
automation: Real PEP limit check with the tenant policy source; the channel adapter is the substituted boundary and exposes the counter. Window arithmetic uses the frozen clock, not sleeps.
prerequisites: Contact-frequency cap is a tenant policy parameter without an owner-approved value; the case is valid only against the labelled synthetic cap.
